title: Midterm Results 2026: When Will Winners Be Announced, State by State?
excerpt: Polls close between 6 p.m. ET Tuesday and 1 a.m. ET Wednesday, but mail-ballot rules mean House and Senate control may not be settled for days.
body:
• Voting in the US midterms is on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The first polls close at 6 p.m. ET in parts of Indiana and Kentucky; the last, in Alaska, close at 1 a.m. ET on Wednesday.
  • Many races will be called on election night, but control of the House or Senate may not be clear until Wednesday or later, NewsNation reported.
  • States certify results between November 10 and December 18, 2026 — election-night numbers are projections, not official results.
  • For Indian-American voters: the races that decide immigration policy may be among the slowest to settle — California counts mail ballots postmarked by Election Day for up to seven days.

If you are planning your Tuesday night around the midterm results, plan for a long one. Polls close state by state between 6 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday, November 3 and 1 a.m. Eastern on Wednesday, and while dozens of races will be called on the night, NewsNation reported that control of the House or Senate may not be clear until Wednesday or later.

Election night, hour by hour

The first results arrive after 6 p.m. ET, when polls close in parts of Indiana and Kentucky. Georgia, Virginia, South Carolina and Vermont follow at 7 p.m.; North Carolina and Ohio at 7:30 p.m.; a large 8 p.m. wave includes Florida, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Maryland; Arizona, New York, Michigan, Texas and Wisconsin close at 9 p.m.; Nevada and Utah at 10 p.m.; California, Oregon and Washington at 11 p.m.; Hawaii at midnight; and Alaska's last precincts at 1 a.m. ET, according to the state-by-state guide at Congress Countdown, compiled from NCSL and Ballotpedia rules as of October 22.

https://x.com/BullTheoryio/status/2116966320067710988

Why some states report fast and others crawl

The difference is mail ballots. States that process mail ballots before Election Day — Florida and Georgia among them — can post totals quickly. Pennsylvania cannot open mail envelopes until Election Day, so its mail count runs late, and Wisconsin processes mail only on Election Day. At the other end, Nevada accepts ballots postmarked by Election Day that arrive within four days, California within seven days, and Alaska counts mailed ballots for 10 days before its ranked-choice tally.

That is why recent history is a warning against early conclusions: in the 2022 midterms, the Senate was not decided until the Saturday after Election Day and the House until the following Wednesday.

Projections are not results

News organizations such as the Associated Press project winners when the remaining uncounted votes cannot change the outcome. A projection is not an official result. States finish their canvass and certify between November 10 and December 18, 2026, and newly elected members of Congress take office at noon on January 3, 2027. Two further dates can extend the story: possible Senate runoffs in Georgia and Mississippi are set for December 1, 2026.

For official tallies for your own races, use your state or county election office — find it through the official-links guidance in NewsNation's explainer — rather than social media screenshots on election night.
